questions.question: What chemical substance is the genetic material in living organisms made of?
options: Protein
DNA
Carbohydrate
Lipid

questions.question: What is the term used to describe all of the DNA contained within a single cell of an organism?
options: The genotype
The chromosome
The gene pool
The genome

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the shape of a DNA molecule?
options: A single straight chain with branching arms
A double helix made of two spiralled chains with links across the middle
A triple-stranded sphere with cross-connections
A flat, circular ring made of three joined chains

questions.question: Why can we see DNA during an extraction experiment, even though individual DNA molecules are too small to be seen with the unaided eye?
options: The DNA molecules expand in water to become thousands of times larger
The chemicals used cause the DNA to glow brightly under normal light
Many DNA molecules clump together in large numbers when extracted
The DNA reacts with oxygen to form a solid metallic precipitate

questions.question: Inside cells, the genome is wound up into tightly-packed structures. What are these structures called?
options: Chromosomes
Ribosomes
Chloroplasts
Proteins

questions.question: How many pairs of chromosomes are typically found in the nucleus of a human body cell, compared to the chromosomes in a bacterium?
options: 46 pairs in a human cell; two pairs in the bacterium cytoplasm
23 pairs in a human cell; one single chromosome in the bacterium cytoplasm
12 pairs in a human cell; 23 pairs in the bacterium nucleus
23 pairs in a human cell; none in the bacterium since bacteria do not have DNA

questions.question: What name is given to the specific sections of DNA in chromosomes that contain the instructions for inherited features and life processes?
options: Nuclei
Proteins
Genes
Hormones

questions.question: What is the function of the non-coding sections of DNA found in an organism's genome?
options: They serve as spare parts to replace damaged genes
They contain instructions that control when the information in genes is used
They provide energy to the cell when glucose levels are low
They prevent the DNA from winding into chromosomes

questions.question: Where is the genetic material stored in a bacterial cell?
options: Inside the nucleus
In the cell wall
In the cytoplasm
Inside the chloroplast

questions.question: Which term describes the biological process by which organisms pass on physical and physiological features to their offspring?
options: Heredity
Respiration
Fertilisation
Adaptation

questions.question: Why do offspring typically show a family resemblance, looking similar to both parents and their siblings?
options: They eat the same food and live in the same house
They inherit genetic features from both parents
They copy the behaviour and facial expressions of their parents
They are identical clones of one of their parents

questions.question: Which of the following types of features can be inherited by offspring from their parents?
options: Only features caused by instructions in the genetic material
Only features that are learned during the parent's lifetime
Any physical change that happens to the parent's body after birth
Only features that are caused by the parent's diet and environment

questions.question: Why can a parent not pass on a scar or a suntan to their biological offspring?
options: These features are stored in the non-coding DNA, which is never inherited
These are features caused by lifestyle and the environment, which cannot be inherited
The body automatically deletes these features before reproduction
These features are only passed on if both parents have them

questions.question: Which of the following pairs correctly identifies one genetically inherited feature and one environmentally caused feature?
options: Inherited: eye colour; Environmental: scars
Inherited: language spoken; Environmental: blood group
Inherited: dyed hair colour; Environmental: natural eye colour
Inherited: scars; Environmental: lobed earlobes

questions.question: In 1952, Rosalind Franklin's team in London used which technique to produce an image showing the structure of a DNA molecule?
options: Light microscopy
X-ray diffraction
Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
Electron scanning

questions.question: How did James Watson and Francis Crick successfully complete their model describing the double helix structure of DNA?
options: By conducting their own X-ray experiments over ten years
By using the picture evidence produced by Rosalind Franklin's team
By extracting DNA from fruit cells for the first time
By using a computer program to generate random chemical models
